title: Harmonic-extension Schur capacity decomposition for phase-conditioned graph gaps
question: Can the phase-conditioned intrinsic graph be decomposed by an exact harmonic extension and Schur complement, so that within-block coercivity and the coarse inter-block capacity give a valid lower bound without the false naive block-gap shortcut?
method: Use the actual finite Q3 conditional momentum conductance from the R-405 grid and form A=diag(pi)^(-1/2)Ldiag(pi)^(-1/2).
Build the weighted block-constant span for lower, neutral when present, and upper q-coordinate sectors, and an orthogonal complement V.
Eliminate V by w_h=-A_VV^(-1)A_VU z and compute the Schur operator S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1)A_VU; use the harmonic-extension mass matrix for its generalized gap.
Check energy orthogonality on deterministic centered probes, use the explicit factor-two variance envelope, and record the safe lower value one half times the minimum of the coarse and residual gaps.
Retain the uncorrected block-constant Ritz value as a hostile shortcut test and apply cross-edge deletion and diagonal-q mutations to expose disconnected or zero-edge behavior.
Run a non-importing reconstruction, hostile mutation lane, integrated verifier and Lean scalar bookkeeping cross-check.
finding: The primary lane passes 4267/4267 assertions over 8 systems, 80 profiles and 1030 conditional rows; the independent lane passes 2114/2114, hostile 6/6, integrated 38/38 and Lean R406 compiles. Full intrinsic gaps range from 0.6310329497027756 to 6.229495058532403. The harmonic Schur coarse gap ranges from 0.634590321876555 to 18.727067154255124, the block-mean-zero residual gap from 2.0000155411351734 to 30.07649788337455, and the explicit factor-two corrected lower envelope from 0.3172951609382775 to 3.232260013170645. The naive block-constant Ritz gap ranges from 0.859366031221583 to 35.521614497313294 and exceeds the full gap on all 1030 rows. In the hostile representative (V=2,d=12,beta=8), the full gap is 3.38789, the corrected envelope is 1.77408, the naive false-lower-bound margin is 1.09327, cross-edge deletion exposes two zero modes, and the diagonal-q mutation has zero edges.
decision_reason: The finite Dirichlet construction repairs the tempting but invalid use of a block-constant Ritz eigenvalue as a lower bound. The Schur correction and residual restriction provide a mathematically valid finite variational interface, while the factor-two variance envelope makes the norm mismatch explicit. This advances the phase-conditioned route without asserting any regulator or thermodynamic uniformity.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite harmonic-extension/Schur-complement checkpoint. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source- or exhaustion-uniform sector bound, phase selection, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

qft_interface.closed: Finite harmonic minimizer, Schur coarse gap, block-mean-zero residual gap, exact energy split up to checked numerical residual, and a safe factor-two finite lower envelope.
qft_interface.open: Uniform Schur/residual lower bounds on a Hamiltonian common core, phase-boundary identification, neutral/cross-capacity limit control, R-399 shell transfer, common alpha and broken-sector GNS coercivity.

adversarial_review.check: Every block column is normalized by its conditional mass and the Gram matrix is checked before the complement is used.
A nonpositive residual spectrum aborts the lane; no pseudoinverse is silently substituted for a disconnected graph.
The harmonic correction is solved from the residual block and deterministic centered probes check E(f)=E(h)+E(g) to the declared tolerance.
Harmonic and residual vectors are not assumed variance-orthogonal; the factor-two triangle envelope is explicit and the finite lower margin is checked.
The uncorrected block-constant restriction is compared with the full Fiedler mode; all 1030 rows exhibit a strict false-lower-bound separation.
Deleting every inter-block edge exposes one zero mode per block, and replacing p by diagonal q creates no kinetic edges.
Finite Schur positivity is not converted into cutoff/volume/source/exhaustion uniformity, common-core dynamics, phase selection, GNS coercivity, a mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

next_action: Prove an analytic source-, cutoff-, volume- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for both the Schur coarse operator and the block-mean-zero residual form on one Hamiltonian common core; identify the coarse variables with a controlled phase boundary condition, then transfer the centered split to the R-399 shell.
no_overclaim: The corrected envelope is a finite variational bound with an explicit factor-two loss. It is not a thermodynamic spectral constant, a phase-selection theorem or a QFT mass-gap result.
